title: Highest temperature in London on May 20?
description:

This aligns with seasonal May baselines of 16–18°C while reflecting subtle springtime warming trends without strong high-pressure dominance. Traders assign the highest implied probability to 19°C at 66.5 percent, followed by 20°C at 37.5 percent, because small variations in cloud thickness or urban heat retention near Schiphol station could shift the exact reading by one degree. Official observations will resolve the market by midnight, with any late-day clearing potentially supporting the upper end of the favored range.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day by the Forecast for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station once information is finalized, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve to "Yes" until all data for this date has been finalized.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is finalized for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent PAGASA forecasts for Manila on May 23 project an afternoon high near 35°C under easterly flow and partly cloudy skies, yet the tight clustering of market-implied odds around 36–37°C reflects ongoing uncertainty in peak solar heating. Key differentiating factors include variable cloud cover that could limit insolation, light winds reducing vertical mixing, and localized thunderstorm development that might cap temperatures below model guidance. Historical May maxima in Metro Manila often reach 34–36°C during similar ridge-dominated patterns, with official resolution depending on the precise 24-hour maximum recorded at the Port Area station. Updated model runs and PAGASA’s next heat-index bulletin will likely sharpen trader assessments ahead of the date.
